blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: cost per GB — Price relative to capacity.

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.text: Magnetic hard disks use magnetised regions on spinning platters with moving heads; they can offer large capacity at relatively low cost per GB.

blocks.title: Apply
blocks.text: Optical discs are read with a laser, often used for physically distributed or archived/removable media, though capacity and drive availability vary.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Flash uses electronic non-volatile memory cells without moving read/write parts; often faster random access and more robust to vibration than HDDs, but trade-offs remain.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the choice
blocks.text: Flash SSD: no spinning platter and generally quick random access; still requires backups.

blocks.title: Explain the choice
blocks.text: Magnetic HDD is a reasonable candidate because of capacity and cost per GB; validate resilience and transfer needs.
